posts.body_html:
Damon of Cali Carnivores once went up to me and showed me a gigantic trap on his black veined flava from Bulloch Co, GA. It's not everyday that you see gigantic traps on these plants, so his accomplishment was a sign of horticultural excellence. As he carried the plant in to show me, he said "Hey mike, check out this plant from Bulloch Effin County, GA!!!!" The way he said it, it reminded me of the scene in Forest Gump when Forest explains that Jenny needs to go back to Greenbow,[insert obscenity] ALABAMA! It's too bad Tommy Hanks didn't swear in this scene:



Now that this somewhat nonsequitur reference has been put to rest, let's talk about the plants! Sadly, we can no longer take pics of these plants in the wild, all we get to see is what's left in cultivation. Some new photos of the various flava forms from Bulloch Co, GA, photos taken 5/9/19, the first picture shows more of a "wildtype" version of the black veined flava. In comparison, you can tell so much work has been done to refine the famous improved black veined plant:


Wildtype:






Improved black veins flava ornata specimen for comparison:



rugelii/ornata integrades:










The regular flava rugelii from Bulloch Co, GA is pretty interesting:

posts.body_html:
It is so sad to see that sites still disappear!

Whenever you go out, you will understand, that we can only collect a few clones, but there are so much variation’s and clones we never can conserve!

So please, we all should fight for conservation of sites and we must stop the global destruction of the few remaining natural habitats!

BT.

posts.body_html:
International Paper, Georgia Pacific, Container Corp, etc. are your chief culprits. The paper companies by far dried up the most wetlands long ago to grow crops of slash and other pine. Before the members on this forum were a twinkle in their parents eyes. Our government owned and operated Ocala National Forest was 300,000 acres mixed harwood/pine hammock now relegated to cropping sand pines. It is the lucrative corporate and government timber industry that destroyed by far the most habitat in the range of Sarracenia. Driving for hours thru pines for hours at a time in SE states ? Those are crops, not natural forests. Pines do not fare well in wet soils. The scope of drainage projects back in the day was massive.

The heavily forested areas are primarily pine crops with the exception of the mountain counties north. Cleared land are urban areas and high production soils for farming.

posts.body_html:
It’s interesting that this just came up about America’s use of toilet paper. I just read up about the famous painting by Grant Wood completed in 1930… which we all know by the name of American Gothic… was originally painted on canvas with an ode to America’s undeniable right to using toilet paper. It was originally called I’m Tired of Corn Cobs.

Apparently once he presented the painting to the woman who would later become his wife of a few years, she quickly noted it’s odd subject matter and insisted he start back over. The marriage only lasted a few years. Wood, late in life, said that he could never forgive her for the toilet paper incident.


Screen Shot 2019-06-05 at 12.33.59 PM by nevermore441, on Flickr
